The API takes one of two routes after checking the cache:

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant Client
    participant API
    participant Cache
    participant DB as Database
    Client->>API: Request
    API->>Cache: Look up value
    alt Cache hit
        Cache-->>API: Cached value
        API-->>Client: Return cached value
    else Cache miss
        Cache-->>API: No cached value
        API->>DB: Query value
        DB-->>API: Returned value
        API->>Cache: Write returned value
        API-->>Client: Return value
    end
```

On a miss, the API queries the database and writes the returned value to the cache before responding. The cache does not call the database.

The web service sends jobs to the queue. Workers take those jobs, write results to the database, and the web service reads the results from the database.

Arrows below show the direction of job and result data:

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    W["Web service"] -->|Jobs| Q["Queue"]
    Q -->|Jobs| R["Workers"]
    R -->|Results| D["Database"]
    D -->|Results| W
```

There is no direct web-to-worker call: the queue carries jobs to workers, and the database stores results for the web service to read.
